subject: astronomy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
questions.explain: Jupiter is the largest planet, with a mass greater than all the other planets combined.

questions.q: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of which two planets?
questions.explain: The main asteroid belt is a region of rocky bodies orbiting between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.q: A comet nucleus is mainly composed of which materials?
questions.explain: Comets are often called 'dirty snowballs' because their nucleus is a mixture of ice, dust and rock.

questions.q: In which year was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union?
questions.explain: The IAU adopted a formal definition of 'planet' in 2006, which reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.

questions.q: Which space probe made a flyby of Pluto in 2015?
questions.explain: New Horizons flew past Pluto in July 2015, returning the first close-up images of its surface.

questions.q: The four inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars) are best described as which type of planet?
questions.explain: The four inner planets have solid rocky surfaces and are known as terrestrial planets.

questions.q: Which planet has the highest surface temperature in the Solar System?
questions.explain: Venus has the hottest surface, around 465 degrees C, owing to its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere.

questions.q: Long-period comets are thought to originate from which region of the Solar System?
questions.explain: The Oort cloud is a distant spherical shell of icy bodies believed to be the source of long-period comets.

questions.q: Why does a comet's tail always point away from the Sun?
options: Because of the comet's high orbital speed
Because it is pushed outwards by the solar wind and radiation pressure
Because the comet is falling towards the Sun
Because of the Earth's magnetic field
questions.explain: The solar wind and radiation pressure blow material away from the Sun, so the tail points away regardless of the comet's direction of travel.

questions.q: What distinguishes a dwarf planet from a full planet under the IAU definition?
options: A dwarf planet does not orbit the Sun
A dwarf planet has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood of other objects
A dwarf planet is not roughly spherical
A dwarf planet has no moons
questions.explain: Both orbit the Sun and are rounded by gravity, but a dwarf planet has not cleared its orbit of other bodies.

questions.q: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury even though it is farther from the Sun?
options: Venus rotates much faster than Mercury
Venus has a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat
Venus is made of hotter rock
questions.explain: Venus's dense CO2 atmosphere produces a strong greenhouse effect, whereas Mercury has almost no atmosphere to retain heat.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of using robotic space probes instead of crewed spacecraft?
options: They can make independent decisions faster than humans
There is no risk to human life and no need for life-support systems
They always return samples to Earth
questions.explain: Probes avoid risking astronauts and do not need costly life-support, making them cheaper and safer for hostile environments.

questions.q: At which point in its orbit does a comet travel fastest?
options: At aphelion, farthest from the Sun
At perihelion, closest to the Sun
At a constant speed throughout its orbit
questions.explain: A comet moves fastest at perihelion because it is closest to the Sun where the gravitational pull is strongest.

questions.q: Why is a robotic probe preferred over astronauts for exploring the surface of Venus?
options: Venus is too far for radio signals to reach
The extreme temperature and crushing pressure would quickly kill astronauts
Astronauts cannot see in Venus's atmosphere
Venus has no solid surface to land on
questions.explain: Venus's surface conditions are far too hostile for humans, so only hardened robotic probes can operate there.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts a typical asteroid with a typical comet?
options: Asteroids are icy while comets are rocky
Asteroids are rocky or metallic while comets are icy and develop tails near the Sun
Both always have long visible tails
Comets orbit within the asteroid belt while asteroids do not orbit the Sun
questions.explain: Asteroids are rocky/metallic bodies, whereas comets are icy and grow a coma and tail as they approach the Sun.

questions.q: Why does a comet only display a bright tail when it is near the Sun?
options: The Sun's light reflects off its solid surface
Heat from the Sun sublimates its ices, releasing gas and dust that form the tail
The Earth is closer to it at that time
Its rotation speeds up near the Sun
questions.explain: Near the Sun the comet's ices vaporise, producing the coma and tail; far away it stays a dark, inactive nucleus.

questions.q: An object orbits the Sun and is large enough to be nearly spherical, but its orbit is shared with many other similar bodies. How should it be classified?
questions.explain: It meets the round and Sun-orbiting criteria but has not cleared its orbit, so it is a dwarf planet.

questions.q: A mission aims to study Saturn's atmosphere, rings and moons continuously over several years. Which type of probe is most suitable?
questions.explain: An orbiter remains in orbit for years, allowing sustained study, as the Cassini mission did at Saturn.

questions.q: A planet is described as rocky, roughly Earth-sized, with a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere and a surface temperature near 465 degrees C. Which planet is it?
questions.explain: These characteristics, especially the dense CO2 atmosphere and extreme heat, identify the planet as Venus.

questions.q: A comet passed perihelion in 1986 and has an orbital period of 75 years. In roughly which year will it next reach perihelion?
questions.explain: Adding the 75-year period to 1986 gives a next perihelion of about 2061, matching Halley's Comet.
